summary: This is an excerpt from a novel (Book 12, part 17) in which Lexy, addressed as Miss Moran, is taken into a house by Mrs. Enderby, who insists Lexy is not Caroline and sends her upstairs to Caroline's bedroom. Lexy removes Caroline's hat and coat and resolves to find Caroline no matter what others think, spending her remaining money to do so. The note also contains one sentence about Megan viewing Monet's 'Impression, Sunrise' in 2013, which appears unrelated to the story and looks like a stray insertion.
one_line: An excerpt from a novel in which Lexy, sent upstairs by Mrs. Enderby, resolves to find the missing Caroline.
key_facts: Mrs. Enderby tells Miss Craigie that 'it's not Caroline' and asks her to let Miss Moran go upstairs.
Mrs. Enderby has a chauffeur carry a small trunk upstairs while Lexy is told to turn her back and look out of the window.
Mrs. Enderby catches Lexy by the shoulder and says 'Take off those things of my child's. Have you no heart?'
Miss Craigie leads Lexy up the stairs to a neat, prim little bedroom where the trunk stands already unlocked.
Lexy takes off Caroline's hat and coat and lays them on the bed.
Lexy says aloud, 'I'm going to find her!' and declares she does not care what anyone else thinks.
Lexy has a little money due to her and intends to use every penny of it in finding Caroline.
Lexy's earlier 'mawkish self-pity' has vanished, and she no longer cares about Mrs. Enderby's attitude toward her.
Miss Craigie is described as bewildered and in the habit of obeying Mrs. Enderby.
Mrs. Enderby is standing in the tiny hall at the end of the excerpt.
A stray sentence in the note states that in 2013, after waiting in line for hours, Megan finally saw the original 'Impression, Sunrise' painting up close.
